title: Set-sheaf equivalence for the internal group action site
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small site $(C,J)$ with finite limits [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$. For a sheaf of groups $K$ with $\mathcal V$-small values, let $\mathscr E^K$ be the category of sheaves of sets $X$ with a natural left action $K\times X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws; its maps are equivariant sheaf maps. Let $C_K$ have the objects of $C$, arrows $(f,a):V\to U$ with $a\in K(V)$, composition $(f,a)\circ(g,b)=(fg,bg^*a)$, and the topology generated by underlying $J$-covering families [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. The formula $E_K(X)(U)=X(U)$, $E_K(X)(f,a)(x)=a\cdot f^*x$, with unchanged components on maps, defines an equivalence $E_K:\mathscr E^K\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(C_K)$. Its inverse sends $N$ to the base sheaf with restriction $N(f,1)$ and action $a\cdot x=N(1_U,a)(x)$; these formulas already give inverse constructions on presheaves and on morphisms. For a sieve $S$ of $C_K$, put $S_1=\{f\mid(f,1)\in S\}$. Matching families for $E_K(X)$ on $S$ are identified with base matching families on $S_1$ by $x_{(f,a)}=a\cdot x_{(f,1)}$. This identification carries unique amalgamations to unique amalgamations. A base presheaf satisfies the covering-family sheaf condition if and only if it satisfies the matching-family condition for every sieve of the topology generated by $J$ [def-weil-pbc-topos]. In particular $E_K(X)$ is a sheaf exactly when $X$ is a base sheaf, and $\mathscr E^K$ has this $\mathcal V$-small-site presentation.

proof.text: Construct extendSet with section set X(U) and restriction along (f,a) equal to a acting on f*x. Its identity law is the unit action law. For composition, naturality and the action law identify b acting on g*(a acting on f*x) with (b g*a) acting on (fg)*x. Construct extendSetMap with the original component maps; naturality is equivariance followed by base naturality. The category and composition are the existing ones of [def-sfb-internal-action-site-basic].

proof.text: For a sieve S, precompose by the invertible vertical arrow labeled a inverse to show that S(f,a) is equivalent to S(f,1); precomposing by a gives the reverse implication. normalizeFamily evaluates a compatible family on (f,1); compatibility along (g,1) gives base compatibility. Conversely extendFamily sends y to the family a acting on y_f. Its compatibility follows from base compatibility, action naturality and the multiplication law. Compatibility of a twisted family along (1,a) forces its entry at (f,a) to be a acting on its entry at (f,1). These identities prove that normalizeFamily and extendFamily are inverse, yielding matchingEquiv for every sieve, including empty sieves.

proof.text: A section amalgamates a twisted matching family if and only if it amalgamates the normalized family: test twisted amalgamation at label 1 for one direction, and use the forced label formula for the other. Both statements quantify over the identical section set, so existence and uniqueness are preserved. Applying this sievewise equivalence and topology_mem_iff from [def-sfb-internal-action-site-basic] gives extendSet_sheaf_iff. For the reverse passage through all base sieves, lift T to the sieve of all labels over its arrows; its label-one sieve is definitionally T.

proof.text: Construct restrictSet with restrictions N(f,1), and recoverSet with action N(1,a), whenever restrictSet satisfies the base sheaf condition. Contravariance and the existing labeled composition give N(1,ab)=N(1,a)N(1,b), with no commutativity assumption. The two factorizations of (f,f*a) give naturality of this action. The component maps of a natural transformation commute with N(f,1) and N(1,a), defining recoverSetMap. Factorization of (f,a) as a vertical arrow followed by (f,1) gives recover_counit with identity components. Conversely the unit action and identity restriction give recover_unit with identity components, including equivariance. Both isomorphisms are natural and satisfy the triangle identity componentwise.

proof.text: To see that restrictSet of a twisted sheaf is a base sheaf, first recover it over the bottom precoverage, where its base presheaf is automatically a sheaf. Its extension is isomorphic to the original twisted sheaf by recover_counit. Transport the sheaf property along that isomorphism and apply extendSet_sheaf_iff. This supplies the inverse functor on sheaves. makeSetEquivalence then assembles these explicitly constructed functors and isomorphisms into SetActionEquivalenceData. All its section equivalences and all unit, counit, restriction, action and morphism formulas are identities on section elements.

proof.text: For the base covering-family criterion, use Mathlib Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff directly. A sheaf for the generated topology is a sheaf for every generating presieve. Conversely, write a covering presieve as an indexed family and apply the covering-pullback clause hJ.2.2 to any base arrow. The chosen pullback family is covering, so the assumed covering-family condition applies. Sieve.ofArrows_eq_pullback_of_isPullback identifies its generated sieve with the pullback of the original generated sieve, and Presieve.isSheafFor_iff_generate gives precisely the generator criterion. This avoids imposing stronger global pretopology or stability-of-all-choices axioms.

Its hypotheses are identical to the item's. Steps 2-4: I checked by hand the contravariance b·g*(a·f*x)=(b g*a)·(fg)*x, the left-action order (1,b)∘(1,a)=(1,ab), naturality via (1,a)∘(f,1)=(f,f*a)=(f,1)∘(1,f*a), and the factorization (f,a)=(f,1)∘(1,a). Step 7 applies lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition (Stacks 00ZC, read at sites.tex l.11244) only on the base C. Step 8 restricts the equivalence to sheaves: the product K×X is computed sectionwise, and the small category and topology from step 1 give the presentation required by def-weil-pbc-topos. Edge cases checked: K=1, a point site with non-abelian G (C_K=G^op, so presheaves are left G-sets), empty covers, and non-constant K.
